faq.a: Mehmed is associated with the Arabic form مَحَمَّد, whose core sense is mehmed; muhammad (balkan form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Mehmed?
faq.a: Mehmed is associated with Arabic. Mehmed is the Bosnian/Turkish form of Arabic مُحَمَّد (Muḥammad), meaning 'praised'.
Yes — the underlying form مَحَمَّد is Arabic.
Mehmed can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Mehmed should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Muḥammad is not a Quranic personal name, though the root ح م د is Quranic.

faq.q: What does Mehmed mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Mehmed is rendered محمد and carries the sense محمد، تعریف شدہ.

faq.q: What does Mehmed mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Mehmed is rendered محمد and carries the sense محمد، ستوده.
A romanized syllable approximation is meh-med. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Mehmed?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Mehmed, mehmed. Script forms are محمد, مَحَمَّد, मेहमेद.

faq.q: Is Mehmed a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
